title: Epithalamium as drama; the four speaking persons
english: This little book is an epithalamium — that is, a wedding song — and seems to me written by Solomon in the manner of a drama. He sang it in the likeness of a bride who is marrying and who burns with heavenly love toward her Bridegroom, who is the Word of God. For she has loved him — whether the soul made in his image, or the church. And this same Scripture also teaches us with what words this magnificent and perfect Bridegroom himself has spoken to the soul or church joined to him. We likewise learn from this same little book titled the Song of Songs what the Bride’s companions — the young women set with the Bride — have said, and also what the Bridegroom’s friends and companions have said. For leave is given even to the Bridegroom’s friends to say some things — at least those things they had heard from the Bridegroom himself — rejoicing at the Bride’s union. So speech comes from the Bride not only to the Bridegroom but also to the young women; and again the Bridegroom’s speech is directed not only to the Bride but also to the Bridegroom’s friends. And this is what we said above: the wedding song is written in the manner of a drama. For a drama is so called as a story is usually acted on stages, where diverse persons are introduced, and as some enter and others even depart, the fabric of the narrative is filled out from different speakers and toward different hearers. This Scripture contains each of these in its own order, and its whole body is shaped by mystical utterances.
translator_notes: Copy-text Baehrens GCS 33 Rufinus Latin.

title: Not for infants; purify passions before this book
english: But first we ought to know that, just as childhood is not moved toward passionate love, so neither is the little and infant age of the inner human admitted even to grasping these words — namely of those who are nourished with milk in Christ and not yet with solid food. For unless someone has been purified from the affections of the flesh and from the passions of the soul, and unless more perfectly instructed, that person cannot know these words healthfully. Whoever therefore is not such as to come to this book should neither hear nor read it; otherwise it will give occasion for blasphemy to Jews and Gentiles and heretics.

title: Solomon’s three books: moral, natural, contemplative
english: I think Solomon handed down a threefold philosophy in these books: moral in Proverbs, natural in Ecclesiastes, contemplative in the Song of Songs. For in Proverbs he corrects morals and cuts back vices; in Ecclesiastes he discusses the nature of things and shows the vanity of temporal things; in the Song of Songs he leads on to contemplation and joins the Bride to the Bridegroom — that is, the church to Christ, or the soul to the Word. The Greeks also name these three kinds of wisdom ethics, physics, and epoptics. But Solomon handed down first ethics, then physics, and last epoptics, so that through correction of morals and knowledge of creatures one may arrive at the contemplation of God.

title: Solomon the Peaceful; peace and charity
english: Solomon is interpreted peaceful. And truly this book is peaceful, in which Bridegroom and Bride come together into one covenant of peace and charity. For how can peace come about except where charity reigns? And how charity, except where Christ, who is our peace, dwells? Therefore Solomon the Peaceful writes the Song of Songs, that he may bring peaceful people into the peace of Christ.

title: Amor, caritas, dilectio — one spiritual love
english: It should also be known that divine Scripture seems to have avoided the word amor and to have used caritas and dilectio more often. Yet it has not altogether shut out the name amor. For where it did not see occasion of falling, there it also inserted the name amor. And it makes no difference in the Scriptures whether amor or caritas or dilectio is said, so long as the same force of affection is designated. Paul too: Who will separate us from the charity of Christ? and again: You shall love the Lord your God. This love, therefore, of which the Song treats is not carnal but spiritual; not cupidity, but charity.

title: Wounded by love — the arrow of Christ
english: I am wounded by charity. This wound is not of death but of life. Christ is the chosen arrow who strikes the heart of the soul and inflicts the wound of love, so that the soul seeks nothing else but the Bridegroom. If someone has not been wounded by this wound, that person has not yet arrived at the Song of Songs. Blessed the soul that is wounded by the love of God, because by this wound it is healed.

title: Outer and inner human; the Song speaks of the inner
english: But the human being is twofold: outer and inner. The outer human was made from the mud of the earth; the inner according to the image of God. The loves of the outer are carnal; the loves of the inner spiritual. The Song of Songs speaks not of the outer but of the inner — of the soul that loves the Word and is loved by him. Unless someone knows himself or herself as inner, that person does not know what to seek in this book.

title: Bride as church or perfect soul; Bridegroom as Word
english: The Bride in this song is understood either as the church or as the perfect soul. The church indeed is the gathering of the saints; the soul is she who already cleaves to Christ alone. And what is said of the church can be transferred to the soul; what of the soul, to the church. But the Bridegroom is Christ, the Word of God, wisdom, peace, justice — all that he himself is.

title: Purify the heart; bridal words are spiritual
english: Before we come to the text itself, the reader must be warned to approach with purged senses and a purified heart. For it is not of carnal marriages that this book treats, though the words are bridal, but of the union of the Word and the soul. If anyone understands otherwise, that person errs and suffers scandal. Therefore Moses and the prophets and the Gospels must be put first, so that by steps of ascent one may arrive at this Song.

title: Prayer to open the Song; transition to the text
english: With these things thus set first, let us now attempt to explain the very words of the Song of Songs, as far as the Lord has given, praying that the Bridegroom himself, who sang these things through Solomon, may even now speak in us and open our sense to understand the mysteries of the Scriptures. The book therefore begins: Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth. But of this and of what follows fuller treatment will be given in the order of the Books themselves.
